fixed_by: Jiro (agent), 2026-11-09 — `String#to_i` reads its radix, and both numeric prefix parsers skip CRuby's whole whitespace set
note: `String#to_i` ignored its radix argument, answering the base-10 value for every call: `"ff".to_i(16)` was 0 and `"10".to_i(2)` was 10. A wrong answer, not a gate — and `to_i(16)` is how Ruby reads a hex string. The arm now resolves the radix (0 reads the prefix, an explicit base accepts only its own), reads digits in that radix, and reports `invalid radix N` and the arity error the way CRuby does; a radix that CRuby obtains by `to_int` dispatch (a Float truncates, a non-numeric raises TypeError) still gates by name rather than guessing. The same file's prefix parsers skipped only ` \t\n\r`, so `"\v10".to_i` and `"\f1.5".to_f` answered 0; CRuby's `rb_isspace` set also has `\v` and `\f`, and both now share one predicate.
